sense.text:
Assyria had already taken the northern kingdom around 722 BC, and around 701 BC they came to besiege Jerusalem and take Judah, the southern kingdom. Their ambassador talked big: we are going to wipe the floor with you, destroy you and bring you into slavery.

The letter Hezekiah received was a letter of threats. He went up into the house of the Lord, laid it down before him, “spread it before the Lord,” and began to pray. That is what we have to do in trouble.

Hezekiah prays to the God that dwelleth between the cherubims: “thou art the God, even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth.” He owns that the kings of Assyria really had destroyed the nations “And have cast their gods into the fire: for they were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone.” So he asks, “save thou us out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art the Lord God, even thou only.”

Isaiah the prophet lived and prophesied in the time of the kings, and here he is with King Hezekiah. This is how you know Isaiah was a prophet: he was not there when Hezekiah prayed before the Lord, but the Lord told him, go to the king and tell him I heard his prayer. “That which thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard.”

“The virgin the daughter of Zion hath despised thee, and laughed thee to scorn.” Sennacherib had exalted his voice and lifted up his eyes “even against the Holy One of Israel.” We are reminded too how our own people have despised the Lord; yet Hezekiah is praying for the Lord to save Judah from a foreign nation that says it will wipe us out.

“By thy messengers thou hast reproached the Lord”: the messengers brought that letter, and in it they reproached the Lord himself. He boasts that he will come up “to the sides of Lebanon” and “cut down the tall cedar trees thereof, and the choice fir trees thereof”: the tall cedars and choice firs are the best of us.

Carmel is northern Israel. The land of Lebanon belonged to us at one time, and it still does. We are going to take it back too, and Carmel is ours as well.

This is Assyria saying what they are going to do to us: they have dried up “all the rivers of besieged places” and laid waste “fenced cities into ruinous heaps,” and the inhabitants were “as the grass of the field.”

“But I know thy abode, and thy going out, and thy coming in, and thy rage against me.” The Lord says, “I will put my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips.” Assyria was famous for that: when they took captives they would put hooks in the nose and the lip and pull them along. Now the Lord will do the same to Assyria and turn him back the way he came.

“And the remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah shall yet again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.” The Lord is saying, you are not destroying Judah; I am not letting Judah be destroyed. No matter how small they get, they will still take root and sprout. “For out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant.”

Now the Lord answers the king of Assyria through Hezekiah: he “shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there.” “For I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.” He did not say for Judah’s sake, but for his own sake and David’s sake.

One angel. “The angel of the Lord went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand”: 185,000 Assyrian soldiers killed by one angel, and in the morning “they were all dead corpses.”

God killed the whole army but let Sennacherib live, so that he could bear witness and tell his people what the Lord did. Then, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, his own sons smote him with the sword. The rest of that history continues in the book of Tobit.

Christian commentaries tie Isaiah 33 back to this history and keep every prophecy in the past, so apologists love to say it already happened. But the scriptures have dual meanings, and Isaiah 33 is also speaking of today.

precepts.why: “Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.” That is what Hezekiah did. Sometimes we get in situations and fear comes upon us. Whatever the problem is, the Lord knows: go before the Lord and spread it out before him, the way Hezekiah spread that letter of threats out before the Lord and prayed.

Christ said, “every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.” Idle means idolatrous: every idolatrous word. Assyria exalted its voice against the Holy One of Israel, and the Lord heard every word of it.

We have to be mindful of this ourselves. Sometimes we speak frivolous things and do not realise the Most High is recording everything.

This goes with verse 27, where the Lord says, “But I know thy abode, and thy going out, and thy coming in, and thy rage against me.” Here is that rage. Rab-shakeh, the ambassador of Assyria, “cried with a loud voice in the Jews’ language”: “Let not Hezekiah deceive you,” and “Neither let Hezekiah make you trust in the Lord.” He is telling the people not to trust in the Lord.

“Make an agreement with me by a present”: pay me tribute, and come out to me, “Until I come and take you away to a land like your own land.” Remember, Assyria took the northern kingdom out of the land and replaced them with other nations; that is what they wanted to do with Judah.

Then he mocks: “where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah? have they delivered Samaria out of mine hand?” Did their gods help the Samaritans, did they help Ephraim? “But the people held their peace, and answered him not a word: for the king’s commandment was, saying, Answer him not.” Nobody responded, because the king told them not to answer him.

sense.text:
Yes, Assyria did this. But guess who also does it today: the United States of America. To spoil means to rob. Look at what America has done to Venezuela, and Venezuela did nothing to America; at what America has done to Iran, and Iran did nothing to America. They took the oil from Venezuela and control it now, and they will not let oil go to Cuba, so Cuba has had no electricity for weeks: babies in incubators and anyone on life support in those hospitals are dead, and the news does not cover it. When they took down Gaddafi, who did nothing against America, America took all his riches; they spoiled Libya. They took the wealth of Saddam Hussein too.

“Dealest treacherously, and they dealt not treacherously with thee”: nations have not dealt treacherously with America. Iran was called to Geneva to talk about a ceasefire, and in the middle of the talks America bombed Iran; another talk of ceasefire, and they bombed them again; and the negotiator himself they killed in Qatar. That is dealing treacherously. So Iran says there will be no more talk of ceasefire, because you deceived us twice.

“When thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled”: when America stops robbing other nations, it shall be robbed. God has prophesied that he will let the nations rise up against it, and when it makes an end of dealing treacherously, “they shall deal treacherously with thee.”

“O Lord, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee”: that is our prayer, just as Hezekiah prayed before the Lord. We have to wait on the Lord. “Be thou their arm every morning”: our men that go out to battle. And be our salvation “in the time of trouble.”
When the Lord lifts himself up, everybody is going to be scattered: “at the lifting up of thyself the nations were scattered.”
“The Lord is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness.” He fills Zion with judgment and righteousness through Christ, the King of kings.

“And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times.” The wisdom and knowledge of this Bible keeps us mentally and spiritually stable. Our people are cursed with madness and unstable, but we all need the wisdom of God and the knowledge of it to keep us stable.

This is why we are not afraid of what is happening in the world. Everybody else is confused and asking what is going on; we know this is what the Bible was talking about.

“The fear of the Lord is his treasure,” because he loves that thing. The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, and if you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.

“Behold, their valiant ones shall cry without”: the valiant ones of the nations, their generals, their armies, their air force, their Marines, all their top men. “The ambassadors of peace shall weep bitterly.” America sends its ambassadors left and right, and they will one day weep bitterly. Like the ambassador of Persia in the story of Sparta who was kicked into a pit, their ambassadors will start being put to death; Iran says it is sick of their ambassadors, because they trick them.

“The highways lie waste”: from destruction and bombs. “The wayfaring man ceaseth”: you will not travel where you want to go; cities will be cut off.

“He hath broken the covenant”: America makes a covenant with nations, an agreement, and then breaks it and tears up the covenant of peace. “He regardeth no man”: they regard nobody, not even their allies in NATO. Spain told them they could not use the base in Spain for the war on Iran, and now they are angry with Spain.

Israel did the same in Lebanon: it held outposts there since the 2024 ceasefire and went back into Lebanon anyway. What happened to the ceasefire? He broke the covenant.

“Lebanon is ashamed and hewn down”: we see Lebanon today, a theater of war again, with villages emptied and tens of thousands in makeshift shelters. One woman there said she wants to live in safety and stability, and wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times.

“Sharon is like a wilderness”: write this down, Sharon is modern-day Tel Aviv, and Tel Aviv now looks like a wilderness under the missiles, though the news is not showing it. We taught on those very streets in Tel Aviv. Bashan is Syria, and Carmel is in northern Israel: they “shake off their fruits.”

“Your breath, as fire, shall devour you”: when you speak great words, talk big against God and cannot back it up, you are going to eat your words. Your big talk is going to burn you up, the way it burned up Antiochus.

“As thorns cut up shall they be burned in the fire.” This is not the same burning we read of in 2 Kings. This battle is going to be with fire: thermonuclear fire.

“Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done”: we are the ones far off, driven into all the countries. “And, ye that are near, acknowledge my might”: what we all have to do is acknowledge God’s might.

Zion is another name for Israel. “The sinners in Zion are afraid; fearfulness hath surprised the hypocrites”: the hypocrites of our own people, the ones following the false leaders. Look at our people in Christianity: churches where they say they have the holy spirit and act like fools, pastors who make a show of their giving, pastors who take the money meant for a widow. Now even some who call themselves Israelites have taken up the speaking in tongues and call it a heavenly language, mixing the lies of foolishness into this truth. Things are so bad that a racist white preacher can say the black churches should be shut down and come and learn from the white man.

“Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings?” God is the devouring fire; the everlasting burnings are the Lord and his throne. The question is who shall dwell in the new kingdom with the Lord.

This is the stipulation to stand before the Lord. “He that walketh righteously, and speaketh uprightly”: speak what the Bible says, and live what it says. “He that despiseth the gain of oppressions”: oppressors gain money from oppressing the poor, and God wants us to despise that. We see oppression as soon as we walk out these doors, the poverty and the nations exploiting our people and our people getting killed in the street, and our brothers and sisters in the church act like they do not see it.

“That shaketh his hands from holding of bribes”: we have to avoid bribery. “That stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood”: some love to hear evil spoken; do not do that. “And shutteth his eyes from seeing evil”: that is how we must be.

“He shall dwell on high: his place of defence shall be the munitions of rocks”: the munitions of rocks is the kingdom, the mountain of the Lord’s house. “Bread shall be given him; his waters shall be sure.”

“Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty”: we want to see the Lord for ourselves. The King is Christ, the King of kings. Even though we die, we are going to be resurrected and see him with our own eyes. “They shall behold the land that is very far off”: that is Jerusalem.

“Where is the scribe?” The scribe is the recorder, who records history and the things that occur. “Where is the receiver?” The one who collects taxes. “Where is he that counted the towers?” The one who makes the military assessment of a city’s defences, since the towers are where the weaponry and arsenal are kept. All of them are gone.

“Thou shalt not see a fierce people, a people of a deeper speech than thou canst perceive; of a stammering tongue, that thou canst not understand.” These are the other nations, whose languages we do not know. We will not see them as a fierce people, because they shall be subdued and forced to worship the King.

“Thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation”: at rest, at peace. “A tabernacle that shall not be taken down; not one of the stakes thereof shall ever be removed”: you put stakes down to hold up a tent, and not one stake of Jerusalem shall ever be pulled up. Nobody will ever take Jerusalem down again.

“Wherein shall go no galley with oars, neither shall gallant ship pass thereby.” Galleys with oars were warships. These ships are not coming through, because the Lord is going to give us power to take down their navy and their air force.
“For the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king; he will save us.” The Lord is our judge, not the nations. And the lawgiver is Christ, who sprang out of Judah.

“Thy tacklings are loosed; they could not well strengthen their mast, they could not spread the sail”: this is their ships. “Then is the prey of a great spoil divided; the lame take the prey.” The lame are Israel. We are going to take the nations; we are going to prey on the nations and divide the spoil.

“And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick”: the inhabitants of Jerusalem. Nobody is going to be sick; we will never again say, I am sick. “The people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity.”

precepts.why:
Scholars say Isaiah 33 is only about the history of Hezekiah and the king of Assyria and how the angel wiped them out. But the scriptures have dual meanings. Job says the Lord would “shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!”

We all want to know the secrets of wisdom, and they are double to that which is written: you read something, but it has a double meaning behind it. That is how the scriptures are written, and as we read Isaiah 33 we see that duality: Assyria then, and America now.

“Yea also, because he transgresseth by wine, he is a proud man.” This white man transgresses by wine, and his wine is his philosophies and falsehoods, his political policies and his religions. You do not get prouder than this white man, Donald Trump in particular.

“Neither keepeth at home”: America does not keep at home; it is in everybody’s business. What are you doing in Venezuela? What the hell are you doing in Iran? You are in Syria too, occupying their land; America set that man up in Syria. “Who enlargeth his desire as hell”: wherever he goes he sets up democracy, and that country goes to hell, a low state. “And is as death, and cannot be satisfied”: he steals one thing and still is not satisfied; now he says he wants Denmark, and he should take Canada too. “But gathereth unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all people”: America is the great melting pot, all nations, peoples and tongues are here.

“Shall not all these take up a parable against him”: all these remnants of the nations that came here from destabilised, bombed and devastated countries. “Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! how long?” The oil of Venezuela is not his, the riches of Iran and Libya are not his, and he seized Russia’s boats and wealth. “How long?” is Habakkuk asking how long this will go on. “To him that ladeth himself with thick clay”: the clay is the nations he has gathered around him, and they come to live in America and say, I will vote Donald Trump, I just love Donald.

“Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee, and awake that shall vex thee”: rise up from sleep, because they are sleeper cells from the nations he destroyed. They bombed Nigeria, and there are Nigerians here; Somalia, and there are Somalis here; Yemen and Iran, and there are Yemenis and Iranians here. “Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee; because of men’s blood”: because of the murders, innocent men, women and children. The first thing they bombed in Iran was a school full of little girls, ages five to ten; their mothers and fathers are screaming and crying at home. And the same media tells us Iran abuses women and keeps them down: then why bomb the girls in school? They just lied to us. America, mind your business. You killed my mother, my father, my child: that is how you make a terrorist, and there is no forgiveness for that.

This is the same as Isaiah 33:1: “Woe to thee that spoilest”, and “when thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled”.

“If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine.” Wine is a metaphor for the spirit of falsehood and lies. That is the wine the proud man of Habakkuk 2 transgresses by: his lies, his policies and his religions, the falsehood he spreads to the nations he spoils.

“For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them.” They are going to think it is all good: we have subdued the earth, everything is ours. And the Lord says, when you say that, then sudden destruction. That is “thou shalt be spoiled.”

“As travail upon a woman with child”: like birthing pains. One thing may happen today, it may calm down, and two or three months or two or three years later something else happens, coming like a woman giving birth. “And they shall not escape.”

“In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits”: when he is full, because he did all the destruction and robbed the nations, he is going to catch hell. It is speaking of the same thing as Isaiah 33:1.

“Every hand of the wicked shall come upon him”: we read that in Habakkuk 2, the nations rising up against him, and NATO is going to turn on them; it is going to happen. “When he is about to fill his belly, God shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him, and shall rain it upon him while he is eating.” That is the same as Thessalonians said: sudden destruction while they say peace and safety.

“But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am the Lord which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth.” That is what we have to glory in, brothers: that we understand and know the Lord. The nations do not understand and know the Lord, so they do not glory in the Lord.

The Lord exercises judgment and righteousness in the earth, and that is how “he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness.”

“I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” This righteous Branch is Christ.

So when Isaiah 33:5 says “he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness,” it is through Christ, the King, the King of kings, who executes judgment and justice in the earth.

Wisdom and knowledge keep us stable, and this is why that is so important: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart.” Our people are smitten with madness: mentally unstable, mentally insane. We are spiritually blind. And our people are always astonished, always shocked at what is going on in the world.

So “wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times”: we need the wisdom of God and the knowledge of it to keep us mentally and spiritually stable.

“The fear of the Lord is all wisdom.” Brothers and sisters, if you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are. That is why “the fear of the Lord is his treasure.”

“And in all wisdom is the performance of the law”: the application of God’s law. We must not just talk about it; we must be about it and do it. “And the knowledge of his omnipotency.”

This is the flip side of “wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times.” When your mind is not saturated with the word of God, you do not have a stable life. “Having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; beguiling unstable souls.”

Our people have eyes full of adultery and cannot cease from sin, and they beguile unstable souls. “An heart they have exercised with covetous practices; cursed children”: our people are cursed children. Even our children, trained up as best we can, may not walk right with the Lord, as the prophet Samuel’s sons did not; you have to know the spirits in your children.

This shows the people who are unstable in all their ways, wavering like the waves of the sea as James said. “And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars”: eclipses of the sun, lunar eclipses, what they call blood moons. “And upon the earth distress of nations”: we are living in that time now.

“With perplexity”: perplexity means confusion. They said they went into Venezuela because Maduro was a drug dealer, as they said of Manuel Noriega; they said Iraq had weapons of mass destruction and did not find one bomb. Whenever they say it is a complex issue, it is something simple they do not want you to know: Maduro was selling his oil in other currencies and not the United States dollar, Iran did the same, and Gaddafi wanted to. That is the perplexity.

“Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth.” Why are they afraid? We are not afraid, because wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of our times. Everybody else is confused; we know this is what the Bible was talking about. “For the powers of heaven shall be shaken”: the powers of heaven are America, England, France and Germany.

“And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.” Christ is coming. “Then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh”: it is almost time to go home.

This is an example of “your breath, as fire, shall devour you”: when you talk big talk against God and cannot back it up, you are going to eat your words, like Nicanor who pointed at the temple and said he would tear it to the ground.

Antiochus, “swelling with anger,” thought to avenge himself on the Jews, “For he had spoken proudly in this sort, That he would come to Jerusalem and make it a common burying place of the Jews.” He wanted to destroy us. “But the Lord Almighty, the God of Isreal, smote him with an incurable and invisible plague”: as soon as he had spoken those words, “a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him.” “And that most justly: for he had tormented other men’s bowels with many and strange torments.”

“Howbeit he nothing at all ceased from his bragging, but still was filled with pride, breathing out fire in his rage against the Jews”: that is the bottom of Isaiah 33:11, his breath as fire devouring him. “He fell down from his chariot, carried violently”: bad enough he had pains in his stomach, now he was dragged, and his whole body hurt.

He who “thought he might command the waves of the sea” was cast on the ground and carried in a horselitter, “so that the worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man,” and “the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army.” He began to stink worse than shit; his whole army could smell him. His big talk burned him up.

“For every battle of the warrior is with confused noise, and garments rolled in blood; but this shall be with burning and fuel of fire.” This battle is going to be with fire. What kind of fire? Thermonuclear fire.

That is the fire of Isaiah 33:12: “as thorns cut up shall they be burned in the fire.” It is not the burning we read of in 2 Kings.

Daniel prays, “O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day.” The literal example: we were the top nation, nations paid tribute to us under Solomon, David conquered everybody, and then we went into captivity. We were confused, but it was our sins that allowed it.

Bring it up to today: our people go to school and get many degrees, and still are not accepted; now they fire black people with degrees and call them DEI hires. We built places like Black Wall Street and Seneca Village, and they bombed them. You told us to get away from you, we did, and you bombed it; you told us to get an education, we did, and they still mock us and scorn us. That is confusion of faces. I assimilated, master; I’m one of you. Look at our people in the Dominican Republic, and the Cubans: I voted for Donald Trump. Now all that crap is backfiring on them. They have not been touched yet, but they are going to get touched.

“To the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them, because of their trespass.” That is who Isaiah 33:13 is speaking to: “Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; and, ye that are near, acknowledge my might.” We are the ones far off.

What does it mean to dwell with the devouring fire, with everlasting burnings? “I beheld till the thrones were cast down”: Daniel saw America fall, Britain, Germany, France, Canada, Australia, and the powerful nations of the east. “And the Ancient of days did sit”: having no beginning of days and no end of days. In order to sit, you have to have a body; in order to wear a garment, you have to have a body. “The hair of his head like the pure wool”: God is a black man.

“His throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire”: his wheels are the chariots of heaven, what they call UFOs. “A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him”: fire bursting from the throne at all times. You are not just going to roll up on the Lord and say, Lord, I want to talk to you; you have to get through that fire first. It is going to be a kingdom of absolute order and rule. “Thousand thousands ministered unto him”: ministering in fire.

“The voice of the great words which the horn spake”: that is America. “I beheld even till the beast was slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame”: the beast is America.

That is the devouring fire and the everlasting burnings of Isaiah 33:14: the fire of the Lord and his throne. Who among us shall dwell with that?

An example of the hypocrites of Isaiah 33:14. “For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.” These are our own religious and political leaders. Our leaders in this society cause us to err and to sin, because we follow what they say, and it is always against God. You followed T. D. Jakes and these other preachers you see on the screen, and those that are led of them are destroyed.

“Therefore the Lord shall have no joy in their young men”: because they follow foolish religious and political leaders. “Neither shall have mercy on their fatherless and widows.” “For every one is an hypocrite and an evildoer”: they all have the Bible and say they believe in Jesus, but will not do a word in that book. “And every mouth speaketh folly”: they all lie as soon as they open their black lips, and it is not in the scriptures.

The Bible calls our people hypocrites. “Therefore when thou doest thine alms, do not sound a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men.” Christ was condemning the Pharisees, who gave their alms publicly and made a big announcement of how much they gave, so everybody could see. That is what the churches do today, calling out the names and amounts of the seed people sow.

“That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.”

“And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men.” When you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. Thousands of Christians praying in the streets to be seen is what Christ said not to do.

“Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayer.” He is speaking of the Pharisees, who were our people, devouring widows’ houses.

The pastors are doing it today: money was given to a church for a widow, and the pastor took it, and the widow never knew. These pastors are robbing widows, which is what Christ said the Pharisees do, and he is telling us not to do that. “Therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.”

“And shall cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.” That is the lake of fire when the Lord returns.

In that time he was speaking of the Pharisees, but today the modern-day Pharisees are our people in Christianity; they do everything the Pharisees did. These are the hypocrites of Isaiah 33:14 that fearfulness shall surprise.

This is the munitions of rocks. “The mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains”: the highest government on earth, literally. “And shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it.”

“Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways.” “For out of Zion shall go forth the law”: that is what is going to go forth out of Zion. That kingdom is the place of defence of the one who walks righteously.

When it says “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty,” it is talking about Christ: “he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.” He is the King of kings and the Lord of lords.

Remember, it also says, “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty.” Job said, “For I know that my redeemer liveth.” Our redeemer is Christ, who sacrificed himself for our people, the twelve tribes of Israel. “And that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth”: in the latter day our redeemer shall stand upon the earth.

“And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God”: after his death, he knew he would be resurrected, regenerated. We have to know that thing. That is Isaiah 33:17: though you die, you are going to be resurrected and see the King.

“Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another”: it is not going to be somebody else. Christians say it is spiritual; no, Job said I am coming back for myself, and I will behold the Lord with my own eyes. “Though my reins be consumed within me”: though my body be destroyed.

Isaiah 33:17 says, “they shall behold the land that is very far off.” “But fear not thou, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel”: he says that because of the great tribulation; Jacob’s trouble is coming. The tribulation leads into Armageddon, World War III. World War III has already begun, and in the middle of that will be Armageddon.

“For, behold, I will save thee from afar off, and thy seed from the land of their captivity”: because we have been taken captive into far off lands, like here in America. “And Jacob shall return, and be in rest and at ease”: we are not going to be bothered by anybody. “And none shall make him afraid”: no nation is ever going to make us afraid again.

“Therefore shall the strong people glorify thee, the city of the terrible nations shall fear thee.” “For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress”: that is us.

“Thou shalt bring down the noise of strangers”: that goes back to verse 3, the strong people and the terrible nations brought to fear. “The branch of the terrible ones shall be brought low”: their branch, their people, shall be brought low. That is why we shall not see a fierce people: they are subdued.

“Who shall not fear thee, O Lord, and glorify thy name? for thou only art holy: for all nations shall come and worship before thee; for thy judgments are made manifest.” His judgments are his prophecies and his laws, made manifest. All nations shall come and worship before him: the fierce people subdued.

When it says all nations shall come and worship, these nations will be subdued; they are going to be forced to give up their idols and come before the King. “Every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” That is why we shall not see a fierce people of a stammering tongue: they shall be subdued and forced to worship the King.

“Arise, O Lord; let not man prevail”: let not man prevail against us. “Let the heathen be judged in thy sight”: the heathen nations. “Put them in fear, O Lord: that the nations may know themselves to be but men.” These nations must know that they themselves are only men. Selah, meaning it is true.

“There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High. God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved.” That is the tabernacle of Isaiah 33:20 that shall not be taken down.

“The heathen raged”: all the heathen nations, the fierce people of a deeper speech and a stammering tongue that we were just reading about. “The kingdoms were moved: he uttered his voice, the earth melted. The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.”

“Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness.” That is Jerusalem. “Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.” That is the Zion and Jerusalem our eyes shall see, a quiet habitation.

“The Lord is our lawgiver.” Brothers used to get confused over this: “Judah is my lawgiver.” You would think it should be Levi, the priests, but it says Judah. Why? Because the lawgiver is Christ, who comes from the tribe of Judah.

“For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.” So Christ is the lawgiver. He is the one that gave Moses the laws, and he is from Judah. That is why Judah is the lawgiver, and why Isaiah 33:22 says “the Lord is our lawgiver.”

Who are the lame that take the prey? “Sing with gladness for Jacob, and shout among the chief of the nations: publish ye, praise ye, and say, O Lord, save thy people, the remnant of Israel.” The Lord is not saving all Israelites; he is only saving a remnant.

“Behold, I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the coasts of the earth, and with them the blind and the lame”: the lame is talking about Israel. “A great company shall return thither.” “For I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn”: Ephraim was chosen over the northern kingdom.

So the lame that take the prey is Israel: we are going to take the nations.

“The multitude wondered, when they saw the dumb to speak, the maimed to be whole, the lame to walk, and the blind to see: and they glorified the God of Israel.” Christ healed the lame of Israel. The lame that take the prey are our people, healed and made whole, and it leads straight into the next verse: the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick.

“The people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity.” “Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases.” He forgives all our iniquities and heals all our diseases, so that the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick.

“Who redeemeth thy life from destruction”: the Lord can redeem our life from destruction. That is the hope amid destruction.

sense.text:
“If any of you lack wisdom”: if any of you are dumb as a rock, dumb as hell. Some of you do not have the spirit of discernment: right and wrong are in front of you and you cannot discern it. When judgment is passed on someone for adultery, there is always that one dumb brother or sister: I don’t understand why y’all had to put them out of the school, all they did was commit a little adultery. Well, shut the hell up and sit down. They cannot discern.

“Let him ask of God”: pray. Just as Hezekiah laid his prayer before the Lord, pray for wisdom, for knowledge, for the spirit of discernment. “That giveth to all men liberally”: to all Israelite men, liberally.

But give the Lord something to work with. You cannot sit at home eating and pray, Lord, help me lose weight, with a chicken leg in one hand and a steak in the other. Start eating smaller portions and doing a little exercise. Likewise, you are praying for wisdom but you have not opened the Bible; the only time you open it is on the Sabbath, and Sunday through Friday the book is closed. They come to the class on the Sabbath and the rest of the week the book is closed. This is for the chosen few that know what to do.

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” If you are asking for wisdom and knowledge, ask in faith. The one who wavers “is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” “For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.”

“A double minded man is unstable in all his ways”: not some of his ways, all of his ways. If you only read once a week, there is nothing for the Lord to work with.

“Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted.” This goes back to verse 5. The brother of low degree is exalted because he is studying and reading. He may not understand, but he is praying, Lord, help my understanding, and one day it opens up: a brother who said little years ago now speaks and explains what the scriptures mean.

precepts.why:
Ezra’s books were burned, and the Lord told him not to worry. “And I took it, and drank: and when I had drunk of it, my heart uttered understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, for my spirit strengthened my memory.”

That part right there: God needed something to work with. The spirit had to access Ezra’s memory so that he could rewrite the records. If you do not read the Bible except on the Sabbath and pray, Lord, open my wisdom, the spirit comes and there is nothing in there, no memory for it to access and bring to your mind. Like the man in the movie Limitless whose pill opened all his memory, so that he could remember things he had only glanced at.

So when you ask God for wisdom, give him something to work with: read the word, so that the spirit has something to bring back.

For brothers who say they have a reading impediment and their eyes start hurting: turn on the Bible audio. Listen before you go to sleep, and the first thing you hear when you wake up is the scriptures.

“Again, there is another that is slow, and hath need of help”: a brother who is mentally slow and needs help. “Wanting ability, and full of poverty”: lacking ability, and poor. “Yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate, And lifted up his head from misery; so that many that saw it marvelled at him.”

It is not impossible. Give the Lord something to work with; show him that you do believe and do have faith, and the Lord can do wonders. That is the brother of low degree who rejoices that he is exalted.

sense.text:
There is more to that one word in Luke 21, perplexity. It reaches into Jacob’s trouble, when the great tribulation hits us to try us. You can read one word, but if you know the rest of the scripture, you know it is going into this too. People want to skip the tribulation and say, there is war, Christ might come back tomorrow. No, he will not; Jacob’s trouble has to come to pass first.

“Immediately after the tribulation of those days”: Christ is telling us there will be tribulation. “The stars shall fall from heaven”: missiles. “And the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”: the heavens, plural, are America, Britain, Germany, France, Russia, Canada, Spain and the European nations, shaken with war.

“And then”: after the tribulation there is still going to be war. So do not say, there is war, we are going home tomorrow; where is the great tribulation, where is Jacob’s trouble? “And then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.”

“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds.” He is not gathering everybody; he is only gathering the elect. The elect are only the Israelites, not Baptists, Pentecostals, Muslims or Catholics.

precepts.why:
How do we know who the heavens are? “And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved”: bombs. “And the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll”: nuclear bombs. “And all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine”: the missiles dropping out of the sky, the satellites falling.

“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven”: when Christ comes, he will bring his sword down in heaven. Then it says who he is talking about: “behold, it shall come down upon Idumea.” Idumea is the Greek and Roman name for Edom. These are the Caucasians: America, France, Germany, Britain, Russia, all those European nations. That is heaven, and those are the powers of the heavens that shall be shaken.
He shall gather together his elect, and who are they? “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect.” The elect is Israel. He is not gathering everybody; only the Israelites.

sense.text: “I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the Lord.” That should make you glad. When somebody says, let’s go up to the sanctuary, and you sigh, there is something wrong with your spirit.
“Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together”: the same height and the same width, foursquare.

“Whither the tribes go up”: not all nations, the tribes. “The tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel, to give thanks unto the name of the Lord.” The testimony, because the kingdom has always been prophesied.

“For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Those are the thrones of the kingdom: the twelve sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel, and they that sat upon them lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.

precepts.why:
This is the city compact together. “And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth”: the length is as long as the breadth. “He measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs”: by man’s measurement about 1,500 miles. “The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal”: it is as tall as it is wide.

“According to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel”: the size is not what we are thinking. It is not man’s measurement; it is angelic measurement.

“The foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones”: garnished means decorated, all kinds of fancy designs in the walls of Jerusalem. Jasper, sapphire, chalcedony, emerald and the rest: twelve foundations, and each stone represents one of the tribes.

The foundations of the kingdom of heaven are the same stones and gems that the high priest wore. “And thou shalt make the breastplate of judgment with cunning work”: cunning work means fancy; it has to look good. “Foursquare it shall be being doubled; a span shall be the length thereof, and a span shall be the breadth thereof”: the breastplate was square, the same height as it was wide, just like the kingdom.

“Even four rows of stones,” “set in gold in their inclosings”: the gold holds them in. “And the stones shall be with the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names, like the engravings of a signet; every one with his name shall they be according to the twelve tribes.” These stones are the names of the children of Israel, and Revelation 21 says the same thing about the foundations of the kingdom.

“And had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” Revelation is saying the same thing as the breastplate of Exodus 28. So the kingdom is not for everybody: the city compact together is built on the twelve tribes, and it is the tribes who go up to it.

“There are set thrones of judgment.” Christ said, “That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” Those are the thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.

“And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them.” “The souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus”: that is the great tribulation. “Which had not worshipped the beast”: which had not worshipped this white man and his kingdom. “Neither his image”: his religion, his politics. “Neither had received his mark upon their foreheads”: had not received his lies in our foreheads, our minds.

“And they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.” Those are the set thrones of judgment.

sense.text: “I will bring my people again from the depths of the sea”: because God’s people are not in the holy land. “That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies”: our foot shall be dipped in the blood of our enemies. “And the tongue of thy dogs in the same”: the nations that run their mouths are our enemies, and it will be the same with them.

“They have seen thy goings, O God; even the goings of my God, my King, in the sanctuary.” “The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after”: people singing beautiful songs before the Lord, not like these churches, and behind them men and women playing instruments, young damsels with timbrels.
“Bless ye God in the congregations, even the Lord, from the fountain of Israel.” The fountain of Israel is Christ.

“There is little Benjamin with their ruler.” Why little Benjamin? Because they were almost wiped out, and they were the youngest tribe, the baby tribe. Then the princes of Judah, of Zebulun and of Naphtali: this is his reestablished kingdom.
“Because of thy temple at Jerusalem shall kings bring presents unto thee”: tribute.

“Rebuke the company of spearmen”: rebuke the soldiers. “The multitude of the bulls”: the people with power in the other nations. “With the calves of the people”: their little ones. “Till every one submit himself with pieces of silver”: till every nation submits and brings us tribute.

“Scatter thou the people that delight in war.” You know who that is: the white man. If there is no war, he will make one; if there is peace on earth, he will undo it. They changed the Department of Defense to the Department of War.

precepts.why:
This proves who the people are that delight in war. “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man; Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” You do not see Trump and them delighting in war? You thought it would end with Venezuela; then Iran; and next they speak of Mexico and maybe Cuba. The party is not over.

“They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent”: the things they say, mocking the nations, as they mock Spain now for refusing them. “Adders’ poison is under their lips”: their philosophies, their religions, their politics. Selah, meaning it is true.

“Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked”: from this so-called white man. “Who have purposed to overthrow my goings”: they purposed to overthrow the goings of the children of Israel. “The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net by the wayside; they have set gins for me”: traps all around us. Selah.

sense.text: “For the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations”: his righteous anger. “And his fury upon all their armies: he hath utterly destroyed them.” He is not destroying everybody yet: he destroys their armies, and there are still going to be the rest of the people. “He hath delivered them to the slaughter.”
“Their slain also shall be cast out, and their stink shall come up out of their carcases”: like Antiochus Epiphanes, whose stink was noisome to all his army.

“And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved”: through thermonuclear destruction, the fire of God. “And the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll”: that is the mushroom cloud. “And all their host shall fall down”: their missiles and satellites. “As the leaf falleth off from the vine”: unexpectedly. They are going to be shooting rockets, their power will be gone, and the rockets will just drop to the ground.

“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea.” Idumea, Edom, is right now in their heaven, and Christ is going to go and destroy them. “And upon the people of my curse”: that is them.

“The sword of the Lord is filled with blood”, “with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams.” These lambs, goats and rams are the nations; he describes them as a sacrifice. “For the Lord hath a sacrifice in Bozrah”: the war he is entering is a major sacrifice. Bozrah is modern-day Jordan, in the land of Edom, and that is where all the wars are going to take place. “And a great slaughter in the land of Idumea”: all the nations will be there.
When the Bible says unicorn, it is not a horse with a horn; it is the rhinoceros. “And their land shall be soaked with blood.”

“For it is the day of the Lord’s vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion.” Everybody wants to know whom that land belongs to. We are living the controversy of Zion: Amalek is saying it is their land. Ask them for a DNA check and they get mad, because you would need the DNA of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob to verify it, and that is not on file.

“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read.” Wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of our times, so we must all get into the habit of consistently reading, four chapters a day at minimum.

“No one of these shall fail”: not one promise in this Bible, not one prophecy, shall fail. “None shall want her mate”: you cannot mate the Bible with any other book. Those in Islam try to mix the Quran with the Bible, and God says you cannot.

“For my mouth it hath commanded”: God’s mouth is the mouth that commanded these words to be written, that commanded us to seek out of the book of the Lord and read, and that said no one of these shall fail. “And his spirit it hath gathered them”: God’s spirit gathered these words together.

“And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line.” As he divided the land of Israel by line, the prophets were given lines to write, some larger portions than others: Obadiah, Micah, Amos, Jonah and Nahum had small portions; Isaiah, Jeremiah and Ezekiel had big portions, and David a big portion in the Psalms.

“They shall possess it for ever, from generation to generation shall they dwell therein.” Just as we shall possess the land forever, we shall possess God’s word forever; as we will dwell in the land forever, we will dwell in the book of the Lord forever.

precepts.why: No one of these shall fail. “Blessed be the Lord, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised: there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.” Not one word of his promise failed then, and not one prophecy shall fail now.

“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read” is the same thing Paul tells Timothy: “Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.” Read, brothers and sisters; give attendance to reading.

“Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery”: the presbytery is the congregation. Just as Timothy had the gift of the holy spirit within him, we all have the gift of the holy spirit within us. Do not let anybody tell you that to show the gift you have to speak in tongues. John the Baptist had the holy spirit, anointed in his mother’s womb, and he did not speak in tongues. Stop listening to these Christians.
